meta.pageTitle: Bible Study — October 4 | Heaven on Earth
meta.title: Heaven on Earth:
meta.footer: Bible Study — October 4  ·  Ordinary Glory: Heaven on Earth  ·  Scripture from the NIV

summary.speaker: Pastor Chris
summary.bigIdea: When we set our minds on heaven, we learn to live, grieve, and love differently on earth.
summary.overview: Pastor Chris begins a series about heaven. He remembers his grandfather, a pastor who spent thousands of hours thinking about heaven and faced the end of his life with peace. He invites us to give heaven more thought, and he explains why a better picture of it matters.

points.title: Imagining Heaven
points.text: Paul asks us to set our minds on things above. Most of us have thought very little about heaven. Knowing that our days are numbered helps us value each one.

points.title: Citizens of Heaven
points.text: Our deepest citizenship is in heaven, but this does not make earth unimportant. God is renewing the earth, so we are more like owners than renters. Hope for heaven sends us to care for people here.

points.title: A Better Picture of Heaven
points.text: Heaven is not clouds and harp music. It is more like our best moments with God and the people we love. Revelation describes a city where God lives with us, every tear is wiped away, and people from every nation walk in his light.

points.title: Living Differently on Earth
points.text: Early Christians cared for the sick because they believed death does not have the last word. Hope in the resurrection lets us grieve with hope and join God’s work to bring his will on earth as it is in heaven.

summary.takeaway: This week, spend a few minutes imagining heaven, and then bring a little of it to someone near you.

col3.text: “Since, then, you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things. For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God. When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with him in glory.”

ps90.text: “Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.”

phil3.text: “But our citizenship is in heaven. And we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ, who, by the power that enables him to bring everything under his control, will transform our lowly bodies so that they will be like his glorious body.”

rev21a.text: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and there was no longer any sea. I saw the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband. And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, ‘Look! God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.’ He who was seated on the throne said, ‘I am making everything new!’ Then he said, ‘Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true.’”

rev21b.text: “I did not see a temple in the city, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. The city does not need the sun or the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and the Lamb is its lamp. The nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth will bring their splendor into it. On no day will its gates ever be shut, for there will be no night there. The glory and honor of the nations will be brought into it.”

cor15.text: “When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come true: ‘Death has been swallowed up in victory.’ ‘Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?’ The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.”

matt6.text: “This, then, is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.’”

lewis.name: C.S. Lewis
lewis.quote: Aim at Heaven and you will get earth ‘thrown in’: aim at earth and you will get neither.

wright.name: N.T. Wright
wright.quote: Heaven is important, but it’s not the end of the world.

romero.name: Oscar Romero
romero.quote: As a Christian, I do not believe in death without resurrection.

buechner.name: Frederick Buechner
buechner.quote: Here is the world. Beautiful and terrible things will happen. Don’t be afraid.

roy.name: Arundhati Roy
roy.quote: Another world is not only possible, she is on her way. On a quiet day, I can hear her breathing.

questions.text: What is one song that has shaped the way you picture heaven?
Think of someone you admire who lived as if each day mattered. What did you notice about them?
How might remembering that you are a citizen of heaven change the way you treat the people around you?
What is one way hope for heaven could make a person more helpful on earth, not less?
Think of a time around a table with people you love that felt like a small taste of heaven. What made it special?
What is one way you could get to know someone from a different background this month?
How might hope in the resurrection change the way a community supports people who are grieving?
What is one small way you could bring a little of heaven to a place near you, like a street, school, or workplace?

prayer.label: Closing Prayer
prayer.text:
Dear God,

Thank you for the hope of heaven. Help us to set our hearts and our minds on things above, and teach us to number our days so that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

Thank you that our citizenship is in heaven. Help us to care for this earth and for every person on it, knowing that you are making all things new.

Give us a better picture of heaven: a place where you live with us, where every tear is wiped away, and where people from every nation walk in your light.

Thank you that death does not have the final word. Comfort those who grieve, and help us to bring a little of your kingdom to the places around us this week, on earth as it is in heaven.

We ask this in the name of Jesus. Amen.
prayer.source: — Based on this week’s study: imagining heaven, citizens of heaven, a better picture of heaven, and living differently on earth.
